newsitem.title: USA: AMR mulls options in stalled BA alliance.
newsitem.headline: AMR mulls options in stalled BA alliance.

text.p: AMR Corp chief executive officer Robert Crandall on Wednesday said American Airlines could press ahead on a limited alliance with British Airways Plc if U.S. and European regulators continue to hold up the deal.
Crandall said AMR's American Airlines and British Airways do not need regulatory approval for several elements of the proposed alliance such as code sharing.
"We can do a big piece of what we seek to do without approval from anyone," Crandall told reporters after AMR's annual shareholders meeting in Dallas.
"We continue to expect that our partnership in one form or another will be implemented in the not-too-distant future," he said.

Senior officials at the European Commission have opposed the proposed alliance, saying it would harm international competition in the airline industry. There also has been opposition to the deal from rival U.S. airlines and consumer groups.
Crandall said European and U.S. regulators "both look fairly imposing," but the process was being held up by "mindless objections (from rival carriers) to every conceivable aspect of the deal."
Crandall said American and BA will wait "as long as it seems sensible to wait" for approval from regulators.
"When we reach the point where it is not likely that further progress is going to be made, we and BA will look for an alternative," he said.
